units.left_text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are in the Dispersion: Greetings.
units.right_text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ,

units.left_text: Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various temptations,
units.right_text: Consider it pure joy, my brothers, when you encounter trials of many kinds,

units.left_text: knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance.
units.right_text: because you know that the testing of your faith develops perseverance.

units.left_text: Let endurance have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.
units.right_text: Allow perseverance to finish its work, so that you may be mature and complete, not lacking anything.

units.left_text: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him.
units.right_text: Now if any of you lacks wisdom, he should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault, and it will be given to him.

units.left_text: But let him ask in faith, without any doubting, for he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven by the wind and tossed.
units.right_text: But he must ask in faith, without doubting, because he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by the wind.

units.left_text: For that man shouldn’t think that he will receive anything from the Lord.
units.right_text: That man should not expect to receive anything from the Lord.

units.left_text: He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.
units.right_text: He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.

units.left_text: Let the brother in humble circumstances glory in his high position;
units.right_text: The brother in humble circumstances should exult in his high position.

units.left_text: and the rich, in that he is made humble, because like the flower in the grass, he will pass away.
units.right_text: But the one who is rich should exult in his low position, because he will pass away like a flower of the field.

units.left_text: For the sun arises with the scorching wind and withers the grass; and the flower in it falls, and the beauty of its appearance perishes. So the rich man will also fade away in his pursuits.
units.right_text: For the sun rises with scorching heat and withers the plant; its flower falls and its beauty is lost. So too, the rich man will fade away in the midst of his pursuits.

units.left_text: Blessed is a person who endures temptation, for when he has been approved, he will receive the crown of life which the Lord promised to those who love him.
units.right_text: Blessed is the man who perseveres under trial, because when he has stood the test, he will receive the crown of life that God has promised to those who love Him.

units.left_text: Let no man say when he is tempted, “I am tempted by God,” for God can’t be tempted by evil, and he himself tempts no one.
units.right_text: When tempted, no one should say, “God is tempting me.” For God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone.

units.left_text: But each one is tempted when he is drawn away by his own lust and enticed.
units.right_text: But each one is tempted when by his own evil desires he is lured away and enticed.

units.left_text: Then the lust, when it has conceived, bears sin. The sin, when it is full grown, produces death.
units.right_text: Then after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death.

units.left_text: Don’t be deceived, my beloved brothers.
units.right_text: Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers.

units.left_text: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom can be no variation nor turning shadow.
units.right_text: Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, with whom there is no change or shifting shadow.

units.left_text: Of his own will he gave birth to us by the word of truth, that we should be a kind of first fruits of his creatures.
units.right_text: He chose to give us birth through the word of truth, that we would be a kind of firstfruits of His creation.

units.left_text: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;
units.right_text: My beloved brothers, understand this: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger,

units.left_text: for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God.
units.right_text: for man’s anger does not bring about the righteousness that God desires.

units.left_text: Therefore, putting away all filthiness and overflowing of wickedness, receive with humility the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
units.right_text: Therefore, get rid of all moral filth and every expression of evil, and humbly accept the word planted in you, which can save your souls.

units.left_text: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves.
units.right_text: Be doers of the word, and not hearers only. Otherwise, you are deceiving yourselves.

units.left_text: For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man looking at his natural face in a mirror;
units.right_text: For anyone who hears the word but does not carry it out is like a man who looks at his face in a mirror,

units.left_text: for he sees himself, and goes away, and immediately forgets what kind of man he was.
units.right_text: and after observing himself goes away and immediately forgets what he looks like.

units.left_text: But he who looks into the perfect law of freedom and continues, not being a hearer who forgets but a doer of the work, this man will be blessed in what he does.
units.right_text: But the one who looks intently into the perfect law of freedom, and continues to do so — not being a forgetful hearer, but an effective doer — he will be blessed in what he does.

units.left_text: If anyone among you thinks himself to be religious while he doesn’t bridle his tongue, but deceives his heart, this man’s religion is worthless.
units.right_text: If anyone considers himself religious and yet does not bridle his tongue, he deceives his heart and his religion is worthless.

units.left_text: Pure religion and undefiled before our God and Father is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.
units.right_text: Pure and undefiled religion before our God and Father is this: to care for orphans and widows in their distress, and to keep oneself from being polluted by the world.

units.left_text: My brothers, don’t hold the faith of our glorious Lord Jesus Christ with partiality.
units.right_text: My brothers, as you hold out your faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ, do not show favoritism.

units.left_text: For if a man with a gold ring, in fine clothing, comes into your synagogue, and a poor man in filthy clothing also comes in,
units.right_text: Suppose a man comes into your meeting wearing a gold ring and fine clothes, and a poor man in shabby clothes also comes in.

units.left_text: and you pay special attention to him who wears the fine clothing and say, “Sit here in a good place;” and you tell the poor man, “Stand there,” or “Sit by my footstool”
units.right_text: If you lavish attention on the man in fine clothes and say, “Here is a seat of honor,” but say to the poor man, “You must stand” or “Sit at my feet,”

units.left_text: haven’t you shown partiality among yourselves, and become judges with evil thoughts?
units.right_text: have you not discriminated among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?

units.left_text: Listen, my beloved brothers. Didn’t God choose those who are poor in this world to be rich in faith and heirs of the Kingdom which he promised to those who love him?
units.right_text: Listen, my beloved brothers: Has not God chosen the poor of this world to be rich in faith and to inherit the kingdom He promised those who love Him?

units.left_text: But you have dishonored the poor man. Don’t the rich oppress you and personally drag you before the courts?
units.right_text: But you have dishonored the poor. Is it not the rich who oppress you and drag you into court?

units.left_text: Don’t they blaspheme the honorable name by which you are called?
units.right_text: Are they not the ones who blaspheme the noble name by which you have been called?

units.left_text: However, if you fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you do well.
units.right_text: If you really fulfill the royal law stated in Scripture, “Love your neighbor as yourself,” you are doing well.

units.left_text: But if you show partiality, you commit sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.
units.right_text: But if you show favoritism, you sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors.

units.left_text: For whoever keeps the whole law, and yet stumbles in one point, he has become guilty of all.
units.right_text: Whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles at just one point is guilty of breaking all of it.

units.left_text: For he who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not commit murder.” Now if you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law.
units.right_text: For He who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not murder.” If you do not commit adultery, but do commit murder, you have become a lawbreaker.

units.left_text: So speak and so do as men who are to be judged by the law of freedom.
units.right_text: Speak and act as those who are going to be judged by the law that gives freedom.

units.left_text: For judgment is without mercy to him who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment.
units.right_text: For judgment without mercy will be shown to anyone who has not been merciful. Mercy triumphs over judgment.

units.left_text: What good is it, my brothers, if a man says he has faith, but has no works? Can faith save him?
units.right_text: What good is it, my brothers, if someone claims to have faith, but has no deeds? Can such faith save him?

units.left_text: And if a brother or sister is naked and in lack of daily food,
units.right_text: Suppose a brother or sister is without clothes and daily food.

units.left_text: and one of you tells them, “Go in peace. Be warmed and filled;” yet you didn’t give them the things the body needs, what good is it?
units.right_text: If one of you tells him, “Go in peace; stay warm and well fed,” but does not provide for his physical needs, what good is that?

units.left_text: Even so faith, if it has no works, is dead in itself.
units.right_text: So too, faith by itself, if it does not result in action, is dead.

units.left_text: Yes, a man will say, “You have faith, and I have works.” Show me your faith without works, and I will show you my faith by my works.
units.right_text: But someone will say, “You have faith and I have deeds.” Show me your faith without deeds, and I will show you my faith by my deeds.

units.left_text: You believe that God is one. You do well. The demons also believe—and shudder.
units.right_text: You believe that God is one. Good for you! Even the demons believe that — and shudder.

units.left_text: But do you want to know, vain man, that faith apart from works is dead?
units.right_text: O foolish man, do you want evidence that faith without deeds is worthless?

units.left_text: Wasn’t Abraham our father justified by works, in that he offered up Isaac his son on the altar?
units.right_text: Was not our father Abraham justified by what he did when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?

units.left_text: You see that faith worked with his works, and by works faith was perfected.
units.right_text: You see that his faith was working with his actions, and his faith was perfected by what he did.

units.left_text: So the Scripture was fulfilled which says, “Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him as righteousness,” and he was called the friend of God.
units.right_text: And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness,” and he was called a friend of God.

units.left_text: You see then that by works a man is justified, and not only by faith.
units.right_text: As you can see, a man is justified by his deeds and not by faith alone.

units.left_text: In the same way, wasn’t Rahab the prostitute also justified by works when she received the messengers and sent them out another way?
units.right_text: In the same way, was not even Rahab the prostitute justified by her actions when she welcomed the spies and sent them off on another route?

units.left_text: For as the body apart from the spirit is dead, even so faith apart from works is dead.
units.right_text: As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead.

units.left_text: Let not many of you be teachers, my brothers, knowing that we will receive heavier judgment.
units.right_text: Not many of you should become teachers, my brothers, because you know that we who teach will be judged more strictly.

units.left_text: For we all stumble in many things. Anyone who doesn’t stumble in word is a perfect person, able to bridle the whole body also.
units.right_text: We all stumble in many ways. If anyone is never at fault in what he says, he is a perfect man, able to control his whole body.

units.left_text: Indeed, we put bits into the horses’ mouths so that they may obey us, and we guide their whole body.
units.right_text: When we put bits into the mouths of horses to make them obey us, we can guide the whole animal.

units.left_text: Behold, the ships also, though they are so big and are driven by fierce winds, are yet guided by a very small rudder, wherever the pilot desires.
units.right_text: Consider ships as well. Although they are so large and are driven by strong winds, they are steered by a very small rudder wherever the pilot is inclined.

units.left_text: So the tongue is also a little member, and boasts great things. See how a small fire can spread to a large forest!
units.right_text: In the same way, the tongue is a small part of the body, but it boasts of great things. Consider how small a spark sets a great forest ablaze.

units.left_text: And the tongue is a fire. The world of iniquity among our members is the tongue, which defiles the whole body, and sets on fire the course of nature, and is set on fire by Gehenna.
units.right_text: The tongue also is a fire, a world of wickedness among the parts of the body. It pollutes the whole person, sets the course of his life on fire, and is itself set on fire by hell.

units.left_text: For every kind of animal, bird, creeping thing, and sea creature is tamed, and has been tamed by mankind;
units.right_text: All kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and creatures of the sea are being tamed and have been tamed by man,

units.left_text: but nobody can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.
units.right_text: but no man can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.

units.left_text: With it we bless our God and Father, and with it we curse men who are made in the image of God.
units.right_text: With the tongue we bless our Lord and Father, and with it we curse men, who have been made in God’s likeness.

units.left_text: Out of the same mouth comes blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to be so.
units.right_text: Out of the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, this should not be!

units.left_text: Does a spring send out from the same opening fresh and bitter water?
units.right_text: Can both fresh water and salt water flow from the same spring?

units.left_text: Can a fig tree, my brothers, yield olives, or a vine figs? Thus no spring yields both salt water and fresh water.
units.right_text: My brothers, can a fig tree grow olives, or a grapevine bear figs? Neither can a salt spring produce fresh water.

units.left_text: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show by his good conduct that his deeds are done in gentleness of wisdom.
units.right_text: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show it by his good conduct, by deeds done in the humility that comes from wisdom.

units.left_text: But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, don’t boast and don’t lie against the truth.
units.right_text: But if you harbor bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast in it or deny the truth.

units.left_text: This wisdom is not that which comes down from above, but is earthly, sensual, and demonic.
units.right_text: Such wisdom does not come from above, but is earthly, unspiritual, demonic.

units.left_text: For where jealousy and selfish ambition are, there is confusion and every evil deed.
units.right_text: For where jealousy and selfish ambition exist, there will be disorder and every evil practice.

units.left_text: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceful, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.
units.right_text: But the wisdom from above is first of all pure, then peace-loving, gentle, accommodating, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial, and sincere.

units.left_text: Now the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.
units.right_text: Peacemakers who sow in peace reap the fruit of righteousness.

units.left_text: Where do wars and fightings among you come from? Don’t they come from your pleasures that war in your members?
units.right_text: What causes conflicts and quarrels among you? Don’t they come from the passions at war within you?

units.left_text: You lust, and don’t have. You murder and covet, and can’t obtain. You fight and make war. You don’t have, because you don’t ask.
units.right_text: You crave what you do not have; you kill and covet, but are unable to obtain it. You quarrel and fight. You do not have, because you do not ask.

units.left_text: You ask, and don’t receive, because you ask with wrong motives, so that you may spend it on your pleasures.
units.right_text: And when you do ask, you do not receive, because you ask with wrong motives, that you may squander it on your pleasures.

units.left_text: You adulterers and adulteresses, don’t you know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Whoever therefore wants to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God.
units.right_text: You adulteresses! Do you not know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Therefore, whoever chooses to be a friend of the world renders himself an enemy of God.

units.left_text: Or do you think that the Scripture says in vain, “The Spirit who lives in us yearns jealously”?
units.right_text: Or do you think the Scripture says without reason that the Spirit He caused to dwell in us yearns with envy?

units.left_text: But he gives more grace. Therefore it says, “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
units.right_text: But He gives us more grace. This is why it says:

units.left_text: Be subject therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
units.right_text: Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

units.left_text: Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you double-minded.
units.right_text: Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded.

units.left_text: Lament, mourn, and weep. Let your laughter be turned to mourning and your joy to gloom.
units.right_text: Grieve, mourn, and weep. Turn your laughter to mourning, and your joy to gloom.

units.left_text: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he will exalt you.
units.right_text: Humble yourselves before the Lord, and He will exalt you.

units.left_text: Don’t speak against one another, brothers. He who speaks against a brother and judges his brother, speaks against the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge.
units.right_text: Brothers, do not slander one another. Anyone who speaks against his brother or judges him speaks against the law and judges it. And if you judge the law, you are not a practitioner of the law, but a judge of it.

units.left_text: Only one is the lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy. But who are you to judge another?
units.right_text: There is only one Lawgiver and Judge, the One who is able to save and destroy. But who are you to judge your neighbor?

units.left_text: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow let’s go into this city and spend a year there, trade, and make a profit.”
units.right_text: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city, spend a year there, carry on business, and make a profit.”

units.left_text: Yet you don’t know what your life will be like tomorrow. For what is your life? For you are a vapor that appears for a little time and then vanishes away.
units.right_text: You do not even know what will happen tomorrow! What is your life? You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.

units.left_text: For you ought to say, “If the Lord wills, we will both live, and do this or that.”
units.right_text: Instead, you ought to say, “If the Lord is willing, we will live and do this or that.”

units.left_text: But now you glory in your boasting. All such boasting is evil.
units.right_text: As it is, you boast in your proud intentions. All such boasting is evil.

units.left_text: To him therefore who knows to do good and doesn’t do it, to him it is sin.
units.right_text: Anyone, then, who knows the right thing to do, yet fails to do it, is guilty of sin.

units.left_text: Come now, you rich, weep and howl for your miseries that are coming on you.
units.right_text: Come now, you who are rich, weep and wail over the misery to come upon you.

units.left_text: Your riches are corrupted and your garments are moth-eaten.
units.right_text: Your riches have rotted and moths have eaten your clothes.

units.left_text: Your gold and your silver are corroded, and their corrosion will be for a testimony against you and will eat your flesh like fire. You have laid up your treasure in the last days.
units.right_text: Your gold and silver are corroded. Their corrosion will testify against you and consume your flesh like fire.

units.left_text: Behold, the wages of the laborers who mowed your fields, which you have kept back by fraud, cry out; and the cries of those who reaped have entered into the ears of the Lord of Armies.
units.right_text: Look, the wages you withheld from the workmen who mowed your fields are crying out against you. The cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of Hosts.

units.left_text: You have lived in luxury on the earth, and taken your pleasure. You have nourished your hearts as in a day of slaughter.
units.right_text: You have lived on earth in luxury and self-indulgence. You have fattened your hearts in the day of slaughter.

units.left_text: You have condemned and you have murdered the righteous one. He doesn’t resist you.
units.right_text: You have condemned and murdered the righteous, who did not resist you.

units.left_text: Be patient therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it, until it receives the early and late rain.
units.right_text: Be patient, then, brothers, until the Lord’s coming. See how the farmer awaits the precious fruit of the soil — how patient he is for the fall and spring rains.

units.left_text: You also be patient. Establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is at hand.
units.right_text: You, too, be patient and strengthen your hearts, because the Lord’s coming is near.

units.left_text: Don’t grumble, brothers, against one another, so that you won’t be judged. Behold, the judge stands at the door.
units.right_text: Do not complain about one another, brothers, so that you will not be judged. Look, the Judge is standing at the door!

units.left_text: Take, brothers, for an example of suffering and of perseverance, the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
units.right_text: Brothers, as an example of patience in affliction, take the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.

units.left_text: Behold, we call them blessed who endured. You have heard of the perseverance of Job and have seen the Lord in the outcome, and how the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.
units.right_text: See how blessed we consider those who have persevered. You have heard of Job’s perseverance and have seen the outcome from the Lord. The Lord is full of compassion and mercy.

units.left_text: But above all things, my brothers, don’t swear—not by heaven, or by the earth, or by any other oath; but let your “yes” be “yes”, and your “no”, “no”, so that you don’t fall into hypocrisy.
units.right_text: Above all, my brothers, do not swear, not by heaven or earth or by any other oath. Simply let your “Yes” be yes, and your “No,” no, so that you will not fall under judgment.

units.left_text: Is any among you suffering? Let him pray. Is any cheerful? Let him sing praises.
units.right_text: Is any one of you suffering? He should pray. Is anyone cheerful? He should sing praises.

units.left_text: Is any among you sick? Let him call for the elders of the assembly, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord;
units.right_text: Is any one of you sick? He should call the elders of the church to pray over him and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord.

units.left_text: and the prayer of faith will heal him who is sick, and the Lord will raise him up. If he has committed sins, he will be forgiven.
units.right_text: And the prayer offered in faith will restore the one who is sick. The Lord will raise him up. If he has sinned, he will be forgiven.

units.left_text: Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective.
units.right_text: Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous man has great power to prevail.

units.left_text: Elijah was a man with a nature like ours, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain, and it didn’t rain on the earth for three years and six months.
units.right_text: Elijah was a man just like us. He prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the land for three and a half years.

units.left_text: He prayed again, and the sky gave rain, and the earth produced its fruit.
units.right_text: Again he prayed, and the heavens gave rain, and the earth yielded its crops.

units.left_text: Brothers, if any among you wanders from the truth and someone turns him back,
units.right_text: My brothers, if one of you should wander from the truth and someone should bring him back,

units.left_text: let him know that he who turns a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins.
units.right_text: consider this: Whoever turns a sinner from the error of his way will save his soul from death and cover over a multitude of sins.
